environment.note: branch derived from 1.4-dev; the modelled tree is 2.0-dev, so absent routes are version skew unless stated otherwise

profile.comment: sacrificial permits image switches, firmware flashes and settings resets; never_strand_mgmt still refuses the 6 network journeys that could move the management address

results.note: full core restart; harness restored the original tag unprompted (the F-063.2 fix working on a real switch)
real reboot confirmed by uptime; back in ~35s
confirmed destructive reset; closes the ledger's settings_reset_partial_failure skip

same 308 as above; its only mutating-smoke step is the pull

eeprom_precheck.conclusion: installed bootloader is newer than the packaged one, so `rpi-eeprom-update -a -d` had nothing to write. The journey exercised the route and the gate, NOT a real EEPROM write. The bricking half of this mode stays unprobed by construction

verification_after.firmware: ArduSub 4.7.0 STABLE (unchanged; ardupilot-manager is in the reset ignore list)

regression_check.negative: passed=24 failed=11 unasserted=28 (baseline on this device was 22/13 — 2 more pass, 2 fewer fail; the newer image serves more routes)
regression_check.smoke_failures: 3 journeys x 2 steps, all 404: disk-usage and recorder-extractor are absent from this image's nginx.conf; network-test resolves to pardal, whose speed-test routes this version does not register (see findings)
regression_check.ui: host-gated to the SITL box at .0.177 (expected skip)
regression_check.conclusion: no failure attributable to the destructive run; a settings wipe cannot produce an nginx-level 404

firmware_info_cold_boot_race.observed: 500 at ~2 min uptime, twice, once with a non-JSON body
firmware_info_cold_boot_race.then: 20/20 HTTP 200 after the MAVLink link settled
firmware_info_cold_boot_race.mechanism: index.py:104-108 requests AUTOPILOT_VERSION over MAVLink and returns PlainTextResponse(...500) on ValueError or MavlinkMessageSendFail
firmware_info_cold_boot_race.implication: probing this route immediately after a reboot yields a spurious 500, and the 500 body is text/plain from a route declaring response_model=FirmwareInfo
